text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Denmark's environmental ministry announced a ban on the future erection of coal-fuelled electric power stations to conform with European Union demands for cuts in CO2 emissions. Industry has expressed concern about energy price rises, in future natural gas will be used in all Danish power plants.

--U.S. secretary of state Madeleine Albright is to accompany President Bill Clinton on his lightning visit to Copenhagen on March 20-21 after the Helsinki summit with Russia's President Boris Yeltsin. First Lady Hillary Clinton is on an African tour and will not visit the Danish capital.

--After IGC, Denmark risks being sidelined in future integration plans for the European Union due to its opt-outs on Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), legal and police cooperation and joint EU citizenship, according to an official Danish foreign ministry note.
--Denmark's research ministry rejects criticism of its proposed telecoms deregulation legislation, notably on interconnect rates for competitors, by telecommunications group Tele Danmark.

--The takeover battle for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix seems set to flare up again this week with Icopal apparently prepared to trump the latest bid by Norwegian Rieber with an offer in excess of 900 million crowns.

--The Social Democrat-led ruling coalition in Denmark seems ready to invite the opposition Conservatives to cooperate on 1998's state budget after studying the thoughts of the new leader Per Stig Moeller on the preservation of the welfare state.
